edges.description: Shown in Drosophila dBRWD3 mutants, where H3.3 levels rise. Not tested in a mammalian system.

Based on a Drosophila genome-wide RNAi screen hit and fly in vivo epistasis, where dBRWD3 is required for JAK/STAT pathway activity; how dBRWD3 acts on the pathway was not determined. Whether BRWD3 loss alters JAK-STAT signalling in human cells relevant to this disorder is unknown.
Shown in Drosophila: reducing yem or H3.3 suppresses the global transcriptome changes of dBRWD3 mutants.
Shown in Drosophila: increased H3.3 in dBRWD3 mutants disrupts dendritic morphogenesis, and reducing yem or H3.3 suppresses the developmental defects.
Proposed. The link from chromatin-driven transcriptional change in flies to human cognitive impairment is an inference by analogy; no human or mammalian neuronal data exist.
Speculative. The human series' authors suggest the H3.3/chromatin mechanism as a possible basis for the overgrowth component, without data on brain growth.
Proposed by analogy. Dendrite defects in fly sensory neurons are taken as a cellular correlate of cognitive impairment; no human or mammalian neuronal data exist.

edges.limitations: Invertebrate model; the H3.3 mechanism has not been tested in mammalian neurons or patient cells.
Dendrite and sensory-organ defects in fly neurons stand in for human cognitive impairment; no behavioural or learning readout was reported.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the BRWD3 gene cause X-linked mental retardation associated with macrocephaly.
evidence.snippet: In the course of systematic screening of the X-chromosome coding sequences in 250 families with nonsyndromic X-linked mental retardation (XLMR), two families were identified with truncating mutations in BRWD3, a gene encoding a bromodomain and WD-repeat domain-containing protein.

evidence.reference_title: Variants in BRWD3 associated with X-linked partial epilepsy without intellectual disability.
evidence.snippet: Further analysis demonstrated that all previously reported destructive variants of BRWD3 caused intellectual disability, while missense variants located in WD40 repeat domains and bromodomains of BRWD3 were associated with epilepsy.

nodes.description: The initiating lesion. Reported pathogenic alleles are stop-gain, frameshift and canonical splice variants and partial or whole-gene deletions, predicted to abolish BRWD3 function. A 586 kb Xq21.1 deletion whose only disease-associated gene is BRWD3 reproduces the phenotype, which supports loss of function as sufficient to cause the disorder. BRWD3 contains eight N-terminal WD40 repeats and two C-terminal bromodomains. Its best-characterised molecular activity is as a substrate-recognition subunit of the CUL4-DDB1-ROC1 (CRL4) E3 ubiquitin ligase, shown biochemically for Drosophila BRWD3 with human CRL4 components; the molecular function binding records that activity as lost.

evidence.reference_title: Null variants and deletions in BRWD3 cause an X-linked syndrome of mild-moderate intellectual disability, macrocephaly, and obesity: A series of 17 patients.
evidence.snippet: The 12 BRWD3 sequence variants included six stop-gain, four frameshift and two canonical splice site variants (predicted to disrupt normal splicing), which were predicted to result in haploinsufficiency of a gene which exhibits a high degree of loss-of-function constraint (pLI 1.00, haploinsufficiency index 28.62%, PVS1).

evidence.snippet: Our patient confirms that the haploinsufficiency due to BRWD3 deletion is a causal genetic mechanism of the BRWD3-related syndromic X-linked intellectual disability.

nodes.description: The only in vivo model bearing on the disease mechanism. dBRWD3 mutants show increased H3.3 levels, global transcriptome changes, and defects of dendritic morphogenesis and sensory organ differentiation, all suppressed by inactivating yem or H3.3. There is no fly readout corresponding to macrocephaly or obesity, and no mammalian Brwd3 knockout has been reported.

evidence.reference_title: Intellectual disability-associated dBRWD3 regulates gene expression through inhibition of HIRA/YEM-mediated chromatin deposition of histone H3.3.
evidence.snippet: Here, we report that dBRWD3, the Drosophila ortholog of the intellectual disability gene BRWD3, regulates gene expression through H3.3, HIRA, and its associated chaperone Yemanuclein (YEM), the fly ortholog of mammalian Ubinuclein1.

nodes.description: Drosophila dBRWD3 negatively regulates replication-independent deposition of the histone variant H3.3 by HIRA and its chaperone Yemanuclein (the fly orthologue of Ubinuclein1). In dBRWD3 mutants H3.3 levels rise, and inactivating yem or H3.3 suppresses the global transcriptome changes and the developmental defects, which places excess H3.3 deposition causally between dBRWD3 loss and the downstream phenotypes in the fly.

nodes.description: Present in every reported affected male and the defining feature. Severity is mild or moderate: 11 of 17 males in the largest series were moderate and the rest mild, and severe intellectual disability has not been a feature of the null-allele series.

evidence.reference_title: Further clinical and molecular characterization of an XLID syndrome associated with BRWD3 variants, a gene implicated in the leukemia-related JAK-STAT pathway.
evidence.snippet: The most common features in males (excluding one patient with a mosaic variant) included ID (39/39 males), speech delay (24/25 males), postnatal macrocephaly (28/35 males) with prominent forehead (18/25 males) and large ears (14/26 males), and obesity (12/27 males).

evidence.snippet: All patients presented with intellectual disability, which was classified as moderate (65%) or mild (35%).

evidence.reference_title: MRX93 syndrome (BRWD3 gene): five new patients with novel mutations.
evidence.snippet: The main features of these patients include ID, macrocephaly and dysmorphic facial features.

nodes.description: In Drosophila cultured cells BRWD3 binds the H3K4 demethylase KDM5 (Lid), co-localises with it genome-wide, and promotes its K48-linked polyubiquitination and Cul4-dependent degradation. BRWD3 depletion raises H3K4me1 and lowers H3K4me3, and depleting KDM5 restores H3K4me3, placing KDM5 accumulation between BRWD3 loss and the methylation change. This is the best-characterised BRWD3 substrate relevant to chromatin, but it has not been examined in human cells or neurons.

evidence.reference_title: BRWD3 promotes KDM5 degradation to maintain H3K4 methylation levels.
evidence.snippet: We show that BRWD3 promotes K48-linked polyubiquitination and degradation of KDM5 and that KDM5 degradation is dependent on both BRWD3 and Cul4.

evidence.reference_title: BRWD3 promotes KDM5 degradation to maintain H3K4 methylation levels.
evidence.snippet: Critically, depleting KDM5 fully restores altered H3K4me3 levels and partially restores H3K4me1 levels upon BRWD3 depletion.

nodes.description: The proposed molecular consequence of BRWD3 loss. In Drosophila dBRWD3 mutants, excess H3.3 disrupts gene expression genome-wide. The authors of the largest human series propose this chromatin-level effect on transcription as a possible mechanism for the overgrowth-intellectual disability phenotype, while noting that no mammalian knockout or functional study exists.

evidence.snippet: Relatively little is known about the biology of the BRWD3 phenotype, and to our knowledge, there have been no reports of knockout models or functional studies in mammalian models.

nodes.description: A genome-wide RNAi screen in Drosophila haemocyte-like cells identified dBRWD3 as required for JAK/STAT pathway activity, and in vivo disruption of dBRWD3 suppressed leukaemia-like blood cell tumours driven by the pathway. The relevance of this to the neurodevelopmental disorder is not established; the node is recorded because BRWD3 was first characterised through it and it is the signalling pathway most often cited for the gene, but no edge to a clinical feature is asserted.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of JAK/STAT signalling components by genome-wide RNA interference.
evidence.snippet: In addition to multiple human disease gene homologues, we have found the tyrosine phosphatase Ptp61F and the Drosophila homologue of BRWD3, a bromo-domain-containing protein disrupted in leukaemia.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of JAK/STAT signalling components by genome-wide RNA interference.
evidence.snippet: Moreover, in vivo analysis demonstrates that disrupted dBRWD3 and overexpressed Ptp61F function as suppressors of leukaemia-like blood cell tumours.
